svg.text: Mooncake Architecture
KVCache-centric Disaggregated LLM Serving - Kimi/Moonshot AI - FAST 2025 / ToS 2025 - github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake
L1 - Production Serving + Ecosystem (Kimi chatbot platform - open-source KV infra)
L2 - Conductor Global Scheduler (KVCache-centric dispatch - SLO-aware overload management)
KVCache-Centric Scheduling
Select prefill + decode pair per request
Maximize prefix reuse + balance load + TTFT SLO
Cache Block Management
Replicate hot blocks - swap cold to SSD tier
Heuristic hot-spot migration without exact prediction
Early Rejection Policy
Predict decode slot availability after prefill
Reject early in overload - predict gen length + load
SLO Metrics
TTFT for prefill - TBT for decode stage
Goodput: only fully completed requests count
Priority + Overload
Priority-based scheduling under peak demand
Mitigate load fluctuation from naive reject
L3 - Disaggregated Inference Clusters (separate prefill pool + decode pool + optional EPD)
L4 - Mooncake Store (distributed global KVCache pool - elastic disaggregated storage)
Paged Block Storage
KV blocks: 16-512 tokens per block (model-tuned)
Prefix hash key: block hash + preceding prefix chain
Dedup identical prefixes across requests/sessions
Object APIs + memory transfer APIs
Context caching API for external reuse
Multi-Tier Cache Hierarchy
DRAM tier: near-GPU CPU memory (primary)
SSD/NVMe tier: larger capacity cold cache
Eviction: LRU / LFU / LengthAware policies
Uses underutilized CPU/DRAM/SSD/NIC of GPU cluster
Striping + parallel I/O for large objects
Replication + Placement Policy
Replica count per object - soft/hard pin
Preferred segments - cache load balancing
Hot blocks replicated to avoid fetch congestion
Elastic add/remove storage nodes independent of engines
Cluster-level shared pool vs per-instance cache
Tensor-Oriented Data Model
Tensors as fundamental carrier across stack
KVCache blocks + model weights + hidden states
Mooncake Backend: elastic tensor compute layer
Hash-based prefix lookup for cross-instance reuse
Open trace dataset with remapped block hashes
L5 - Transfer Engine (TE) - high-performance zero-copy data movement backbone
RDMA + Multi-NIC
Aggregate bandwidth across multiple NICs
87 GB/s (4x200G) - 190 GB/s (8x400G RoCE)
Topology-Aware Routing
NUMA affinity - optimal device selection
Auto failover on transient network errors
Heterogeneous Transports
TCP - RDMA - NVLink - NVMe-oF - AWS EFA
CUDA/MUSA/HIP/Ascend/CXL/Barex support
GPUDirect + Zero-Copy
Batched cross-node KV block transfer
Layer-by-layer stream during prefill overlap
Unified Transfer API
DRAM/VRAM/NVMe tensor movement
Foundation for Store + P2P weight sync
L6 - Framework Connectors (vLLM / SGLang / TensorRT-LLM integration layer)
MooncakeConnector (PD xfer)
vLLM v1 KV Connector for disagg prefill-decode
Prefill worker to decode worker KV blocks via TE
MooncakeStoreConnector
Cluster-level KV pool - hash prefix caching
Cross-instance reuse - agentic multi-turn workloads
SGLang Integration
PD disagg + HiCache remote tier + EPD multimodal
SGLang-Omni relay - RL P2P weight transfer
Other Integrations
TensorRT-LLM cache_transmission utils
LMCache remote - NIXL plugin - FlexKV - Ascend
vLLM-Omni Stages
MooncakeTransferEngineConnector
Cross-stage tensor/blob relay in omni pipelines
L7 - Cluster Resources (pooled CPU/DRAM/SSD/NIC/GPU - trading storage for computation)
Four-Step Request Workflow (Conductor-orchestrated)
Tokenize - schedule - prefix reuse - chunked prefill - stream KV - decode batch
Step 1 KVCache Reuse: load prefix blocks from Store/remote CPU to prefill GPU (skip if miss)
Step 2 Incremental Prefill: CPP chunks + layer-wise compute/store overlap in prefill pool
Step 3 KVCache Transfer: Messenger streams per-layer KV via TE to decode node CPU DRAM async
Step 4 Decode: async KV load to GPU + continuous batching - local TBT SLO double-check
Layer-wise overlap: prefill time approx max(KV load, compute) - VRAM need only 1 request
Cache-aware Algorithm 1: prefix_len match + load balance + transfer time prediction
Design motto: Trading More Storage for Less Computation (FAST 2025 paper title)
Design Position: KVCache-Centric vs Compute-Centric Serving
Disaggregate P/D + global KV pool + RDMA transfer - optimize for prefix-heavy long context
Spectrum Comparison
vLLM standalone
Local prefix cache per instance
Colocated prefill + decode
Disagg P/D only
Split clusters - no global KV pool
Transfer KV but limited reuse scope
LMCache / FlexKV
External KV cache layers
Can use Mooncake TE as backend
Mooncake (this work)
Global KV pool + Conductor + TE + Store
Full-stack P/D disagg for Kimi production
Key Architectural Decisions
KV-first sched
Cache drives placement
P/D disagg
Independent scale pools
Global Store
DRAM+SSD pooled cache
RDMA TE
Zero-copy KV movement
Early reject
Overload-aware goodput
CPP + stream
Long-context TTFT control
Open-Source Components (kvcache-ai/Mooncake)
Transfer Engine (TE) + Mooncake Store + Connectors - Apache-2.0
TE open Nov 2024 - Store open Mar 2025 - production trace with hash_ids published
Design Position (Moonshot AI Kimi platform - KVCache as first-class schedulable resource)
Disagg P/D clusters + global Mooncake Store + Transfer Engine + Conductor - long-context prefix reuse at scale
Deploy: vLLM MooncakeConnector/StoreConnector - SGLang HiCache - pip/build from kvcache-ai.github.io/Mooncake
